collins.hedgehog: Become best in the world at paper-based consumer products (brands such as tissue and diapers), giving up commodity paper; economic denominator is profit per consumer brand.
collins.stop_doing: Sell the paper mills (including the namesake mill) and put the proceeds into consumer products, competing head-on with P&G.
stop_doing_key_points: sell or exit the commodity paper mills
stop funding coated/business paper by default
collins.leader_type: Level 5 (Darwin Smith: humble in-house lawyer, fierce resolve, kept working through cancer)
brutal_facts: the core mill business is a commodity business whose returns trail the market
to win in consumer products the company must take on P&G

later_history: 1971-1991 cumulative stock returns about 4.1x the general market (per Collins), beating Scott Paper and P&G. Acquired Scott Paper in 1995. Closed its last own pulp/paper mill in 2012. Has stayed a large consumer-products company, without a collapse on the scale of the How the Mighty Fall cases.
notes: Track A matched pair with A02 (Scott Paper). Collins's appendix gives K-C's transition as 1972 (window 1972-87); the dossier is dated 1971, just before it.
